title: Uttaradit–Phrae 3-Day Trip: Quiet Lower Northern Thailand | ThailandAddict
metaDesc: A 3-day Uttaradit–Phrae itinerary covering Laplae town, Wat Phra Thaen Sila At, then over to Phrae's old town, Khum Chao Luang and Phra That Cho Hae. Easy day-by-day driving, the two towns sit just 60 km apart.
keywords: Uttaradit Phrae trip, Uttaradit 3 day itinerary, Uttaradit to Phrae, things to do in Phrae, Laplae town, Phrae old town
intro: These two provinces sit right next to each other on the same road, just about 60 kilometers apart, yet most people visit them separately when pairing them into one trip actually works far better. Uttaradit gives you Laplae town and its prized Long Laplae durian; Phrae gives you a teak-wood old town and quiet cafes. This is a 3-day plan that keeps the driving easy, where the crowds still haven't caught up, and that suits anyone who wants to escape the big city and walk slowly for a few days.

blocks.html: Uttaradit and Phrae are a pair of lower-northern towns linked by Highway 11 through Den Chai district. From downtown Uttaradit to downtown Phrae is about 60 kilometers, just over an hour's drive, with most of the road being four lanes and an easy cruise, so pairing them into a single trip fits together nicely. This plan starts with two days in Uttaradit, then flows down to Phrae on the last day, letting you cover everything without backtracking.

items: People with their own car — public transport within these two towns is sparse, so having your own wheels is by far the easiest, since many of the sights sit outside the town center.
Slow travelers — both are secondary provinces with no crowds, so you can stroll and take photos at your own pace without fighting for a spot.
Fans of old towns and local food — Laplae and Phrae's old town have local dishes that are hard to find anywhere else.
Families or couples — the pace is relaxed and there's a mix of temples, nature and cafes, so it works across ages.

blocks.text: Day 1 — Arrive in Uttaradit, take in Laplae and key temples

blocks.html: The first day focuses on the Laplae side, the district at the heart of Uttaradit, with its old temples, town museum and the food the province is known for. Take it slow from late morning right through to evening.

items.activity: Arrive in downtown Uttaradit, check in and rest up for a bit
items.note: There's a range of places to stay in town. Picking somewhere near Samran Ruen Road makes it easy to walk out and find food.

items.activity: Lunch on khao phan phak, Laplae's signature dish
items.note: Khao Phan Indy in Laplae district is a popular spot. It's a steamed rice-flour crepe wrapped around various vegetables, starting at a few tens of baht a plate. Closed Fridays.

items.activity: Pay respects at Wat Phra Thaen Sila At, Laplae district
items.note: An old royal temple housing the Phra Thaen Sila At stone slab, a sacred object that's a symbol of the province.

items.activity: Stop at Wat Phra Yuen Phutthabat Yukhon, then visit the Laplae Town Museum
items.note: The museum tells the story of how Laplae people lived in the past, so you understand the origins of the town's legend before carrying on.

items.activity: Drive up to Mae Phul Waterfall and rest in the cool breeze
items.note: A shady tiered rock waterfall. It's at its best from the rainy season into early winter; in the dry season the water runs low.

items.activity: Head back into town and find dinner around the town market
items.note: Try mi phan (rolled noodles) or noodles at an old shop in town. Prices are easy on the wallet.

blocks.title: About the durian
blocks.html: If you come around June to August, it's the season for Long Laplae and Lin Laplae durian, the province's pride, with fine-textured flesh that's sweet without being cloying. You can buy it at orchards and stalls in Laplae district. Outside the season there's no fresh fruit, so don't get your hopes up in the wrong month.

blocks.text: Day 2 — Uttaradit's nature, then prepping to cross over

blocks.html: Day two heads out of town toward Sirikit Dam to take in the wide reservoir views, then in the afternoon you drift back to catch a few spots in town and pick up souvenirs before your last night in Uttaradit.

items.activity: Set off for Sirikit Dam, Tha Pla district
items.note: About an hour from town. The uphill stretch near the end is winding, so drive carefully.

items.activity: See the dam crest and reservoir views, photos at the viewpoint
items.note: A large earth-fill dam with mountains ringing a wide expanse of water. The morning air is cool and pleasant.

items.activity: Lunch at a riverside restaurant near the dam or in Tha Pla district
items.note: There are several river-fish restaurants. Try grilled fish or tom yum fish, bold local flavors.

items.activity: Drive back into town and stop at the Phraya Phichai Dap Hak Monument
items.note: On the plaza in front of the provincial hall, it's the province's landmark, good for photos and hearing the story of Mueang Phichai's hero.

items.activity: Sit at a cafe in town and rest your legs before tomorrow's drive
items.note: Small cafes in town keep popping up, with quiet, uncrowded vibes.

items.activity: Shop for souvenirs: durian paste, dried fruit, Laplae woven textiles
items.note: Laplae souvenirs can be found at shops and markets in town. Stock up before heading down to Phrae tomorrow.

blocks.text: Day 3 — Cross over to Phrae, the teak-wood old town

blocks.html: On the last day, check out early and drive south on Highway 11 through Den Chai into downtown Phrae, an old town that still keeps plenty of antique teak houses. Walk around Khum Chao Luang, pay respects at Phra That Cho Hae, then wrap up with a cafe and some mo hom indigo cloth to take home.

items.activity: Check out and drive out of Uttaradit onto Highway 11
items.note: Through Den Chai into Phrae town, about 60 km, taking just over an hour.

items.activity: Arrive in downtown Phrae, starting at Khum Chao Luang and Khum Wongburi
items.note: Khum Chao Luang is a wooden mansion from the reign of Rama V with lovely fretwork, while Khum Wongburi is a pink teak house in an adapted European style.

items.activity: Stroll the old town: Pratu Chai, Wat Phong Sunan, Wat Luang
items.note: This area is walkable. Many of the old wooden houses are still lived in, so there's always something to photograph.

items.activity: Eat khao soi or northern food at a shop in town
items.note: Phrae has khao soi and bold northern dishes, with long-standing shops scattered through the old town.

items.activity: Drive to pay respects at Phra That Cho Hae, the stupa for those born in the Year of the Tiger
items.note: About 9 km from town. The golden stupa stands out and the temple is a companion to the city of Phrae.

items.activity: Stop at Phae Mueang Phi to see the oddly shaped earth pillars
items.note: An earth-pillar geopark carved out by water and wind. It only takes a short walk, good to drop by before heading back.

items.activity: Sit at a Phrae cafe and close the trip with an iced coffee
items.note: Many wooden-house cafes in town use arabica beans from Den Chai, with a slow vibe that suits the town.

items.activity: Buy mo hom indigo cloth, Phrae's signature souvenir, before heading home
items.note: The mo hom cloth center and shops in town have plenty of options, both shirts and lengths of fabric.

blocks.html: Here's a short list to slot in along the way. Both towns have local dishes that are hard to find elsewhere, so trying them all is more worthwhile than eating at generic restaurants.

items.name: Khao phan phak (Laplae)
items.blurb: Thin steamed rice-flour crepes wrapped around an assortment of vegetables and topped with sauce, the dish Uttaradit is known for. Khao Phan Indy in Laplae is a popular spot.

items.name: Mi phan / mi khluk
items.blurb: Rice noodles seasoned the Laplae way, eaten alongside khao phan at the same shop, a light meal that fills you up just right.

items.name: Long Laplae & Lin Laplae durian
items.blurb: Local durian varieties with fine flesh, sweet without being cloying, available only in season around June to August. Buy them at orchards in Laplae.

items.name: River fish near Sirikit Dam
items.blurb: Grilled fish, tom yum fish, fried fish at riverside restaurants around Tha Pla, bold and fresh, perfect for lunch on a dam day.

items.name: Phrae khao soi
items.blurb: Rich northern-style khao soi. Several old shops in Phrae's old town have been at it for years, a good bite before walking the town.

items.name: Den Chai arabica coffee
items.blurb: Many Phrae cafes use beans from the hills around Den Chai. Sip in a quiet old wooden house, an easy way to close the trip.

blocks.text: More to see if you have time

items.name: Wat Na Khuha / bamboo bridge
items.blurb: A small community outside Phrae town with a bamboo bridge across the fields and a peaceful feel, good for early-morning photos.

items.name: Vineyard in Laplae
items.blurb: A vineyard decked out in European-style colors with photo spots and snacks, a nice add-on to your first day.

items.name: Ban Na Thong / mo hom village
items.blurb: Watch the real mo hom dyeing process and buy cloth straight from the source at better prices than in town.

blocks.text: Tips for planning a smooth trip

items: Fill up before leaving town — gas stations are spread thin on the route to Sirikit Dam and along some temple access roads, so topping off a full tank in town gives you peace of mind.
Check shop closing days — some local shops close midweek, like Khao Phan Indy on Fridays, so check ahead so you don't miss out.

Winter is the best window — November to February brings cool, pleasant weather, ideal for walking the old town and going up to the dam. The rainy season makes the waterfalls pretty but the roads slippery.
You can put the last night in Phrae — if you'd rather not do a long drive on the final day, stay a night in Phrae and head back after, which lets you see more of Phrae.

faq.q: Is it far from Uttaradit to Phrae, and how many hours is the drive?
faq.a: From downtown Uttaradit to downtown Phrae is about 60 kilometers via Highway 11 through Den Chai district, roughly just over an hour's drive. Most of the road is four lanes and an easy cruise.

faq.q: Do you need your own car for this trip?
faq.a: Having a car is recommended, because many of the sights sit outside the town center, like Sirikit Dam, Mae Phul Waterfall and Phra That Cho Hae. Public transport within both provinces is sparse, so without your own car you may need to rent one or hire a vehicle for parts of the trip.

faq.q: When is the best time to go?
faq.a: Winter, November to February, has cool, pleasant weather that's best for walking the old town and going up to the dam. If you want to eat Long Laplae durian, come around June to August, which is durian season, but expect it to be hot and rainy then.

faq.q: Are 3 days enough for both provinces?
faq.a: Enough to catch the main highlights: two days for Laplae and Uttaradit's key temples, then Phrae's old town and Phra That Cho Hae on the last day. If you want to dig deeper into Phrae, bump it up to 4 days and stay one more night in Phrae.

faq.q: What are the standout souvenirs from each province?
faq.a: Uttaradit is known for durian paste, dried fruit and Laplae woven textiles, while Phrae is famous for its distinctive indigo-dyed mo hom cloth. You can buy both in town or from the source villages at better prices.
